prompt:
Challenge C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
Detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Membrane fouling in dairy wastewater involves formation of compressible gel layers dominated by emulsified fats and proteins, which can be characterized through scanning electron microscopy, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and hydraulic resistance analysis.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08238","field":"abstract","quote":"Fouling layer composition was characterized by scanning electron microscopy, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and hydraulic resistance analysis"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08240","field":"abstract","quote":"emulsified oil droplets constitute the primary foulant, forming a compressible gel layer"}]},{"text":"Ultrasound-assisted in-situ cleaning at 25 kHz can reduce irreversible fouling resistance by up to 62% compared to hydraulic backwashing alone and extend membrane service life without compromising membrane integrity.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08238","field":"abstract","quote":"ultrasound-assisted cleaning reduced irreversible fouling resistance by up to 62% compared to hydraulic backwashing alone"}]},{"text":"Pre-treatment through feed screening at 200 micrometers can reduce total fouling resistance by 34% in fat-rich wastewater by removing primary foulants before they reach the membrane.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08240","field":"abstract","quote":"Pre-screening of the feed stream through a 200 µm mesh reduced total fouling resistance by 34%"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The publications directly address fouling mechanisms in polymeric membranes treating dairy and fat-rich wastewater [SYN-PUB-08238, SYN-PUB-08240], characterize gel layer composition [SYN-PUB-08238], propose practical cleaning and pre-treatment solutions [SYN-PUB-08238, SYN-PUB-08240], and model temperature-dependent fouling dynamics [SYN-PUB-08239], all core to the challenge."}
